app.name: TrimmTrack
app.tagline: Turn your spreadsheet into a live portfolio tracker

home.heroTitle: Your portfolio, always up to date
home.heroSubtitle: Upload your spreadsheet and turn it into a dashboard with live prices, P&L, and dividends. Plus a free FIFO calculator, DCF and Reverse DCF valuation, and the Graham Number — no sign-up needed.
home.feat1Desc: Works with Excel and Google Sheets exported as XLSX.
home.feat2Desc: Automatic update once a day after US market close.
home.feat3Desc: Pick a display currency and we handle FX conversion automatically.

steps.title: How it works, in 3 steps
steps.s1d: Upload your broker's Excel or add positions by hand. If your sheet is messy, we give you a prompt to tidy it up with an AI.
steps.s2d: We fetch live prices, FX and history automatically, and keep it up to date every day after market close.
steps.s3d: See P&L, dividends, performance, evolution and six valuation models — always current.

trust.t1d: Your data is only yours. We never sell it or share it with anyone.
trust.t2d: Prices and fundamentals from Yahoo Finance, refreshed daily.
trust.t3d: Not financial advice: we help you see clearly and you make the decisions.

disclaimer.title: Read this before uploading
disclaimer.important: Important: review your spreadsheet before uploading
disclaimer.p1: This tool expects data in a specific format. If your data is mixed with notes, formulas, or extra columns, the result may be incorrect.
disclaimer.p2: We strongly recommend running your Excel through an AI (Claude, ChatGPT or similar) using the prompt available in the «How to prepare» tab. That way you make sure the columns are the expected ones and the dates are in the right format.
disclaimer.p3: This app is not financial advice. Price data comes from third-party sources and may be delayed. Always verify with your broker before making decisions.

performance.title: Performance
performance.irrHint: Internal rate of return (XIRR): the real annualised return your money has earned, accounting for WHEN you put each euro in and took it out. It's the textbook money-weighted measure. Unlike “Total return” (cumulative), IRR is a % per year.
performance.sinceHint: Total gain = unrealized gain (open) + realized result + dividends + interest. The % return is computed over net capital invested (all buys minus all sells) — the money you actually put in from your pocket, not capital recycled from one trade into another.
performance.needsBackfill: To see the % return for each year you need to download the price history.
performance.byYearHint: “Return %” and “Value gain” reconstruct the portfolio's market value at year-end (includes unrealized gains, ~3 years of history). “Realized €” is closed sales + dividends + interest for that year, exact across all history.

fundamentals.perCardHint: Portfolio average P/E (price/earnings), weighted by each position's value and computed as a harmonic mean (the correct way to aggregate ratios). Uses the trailing P/E from fundamentals; crypto and unprofitable companies are left out.
fundamentals.noneForTicker: No fundamentals for this ticker. Try refreshing.

scenario.title: Scenario valuation
scenario.baseEpsMissing: Couldn't fetch forward EPS from Yahoo. Enter it manually to see the valuation.
scenario.probWarn: Probabilities don't add up to 100% — normalised anyway.
scenario.dcaEmpty: No buys yet. Add one or more to simulate averaging in over several purchases.

dcf.intro: Projects the per-share metric (EPS or FCF/share), applies an exit multiple and discounts the future price at your desired return. The fair value is the most you can pay today to earn that return.
dcf.missing: No base {{metric}} available from Yahoo. Enter it manually or refresh fundamentals.
dcf.negative: Base {{metric}} is negative or zero: this model doesn't apply (no positive earnings/FCF). Try the other metric or the scenarios.
dcf.reverseIntro: The inverse: starting from the current price, what annual growth must the company deliver to justify it given your multiple and return? A great sanity check.
dcf.reverseUnsolvable: Can't solve the implied growth with these assumptions (invalid price, multiple or base metric).
dcf.reverseSentence: The current price implies the market expects {{implied}}%/yr {{metric}} growth for {{years}} years. Do you think that's achievable?
dcf.reverseCompare: You assume {{assumed}}%/yr in the DCF → the market is {{verdict}} than your thesis.

graham.intro: Benjamin Graham's classic interest-adjusted formula. Fast and defensive, built for screening — not a fine valuation.
graham.missing: No EPS available from Yahoo. Enter it manually or refresh fundamentals.
graham.negative: EPS is negative or zero: Graham's formula doesn't apply to unprofitable companies.
graham.screenNote: Conservative screening estimate, not a precise valuation.
graham.clampNote: growth capped at {{cap}}% (the 2g term over-inflates at high growth)

mc.intro: Simulates thousands of DCF runs varying growth and exit multiple. Instead of one number you get a distribution of the {{metric}} fair value.
mc.pointHint: DCF central points: growth {{growth}}%, multiple {{multiple}}× (edit them in the DCF tab)
mc.sentence: The fair value is between {{p10}} and {{p90}} with ~80% probability.

sotp.intro: Value each stake the holding owns and sum them. Listed stakes pull a live market cap from Yahoo (× your stake); unlisted ones use a manual value. Holdings persistently trade below NAV: apply a holding discount so the target price is realistic.
sotp.empty: No stakes yet. Start with "+ Add stake".
sotp.fallback: no live market cap — using the manual value
sotp.useMarketDiscountHint: Apply the discount the market already puts on NAV today

history.title: Portfolio evolution
history.empty: Not enough history to draw the chart yet. Try downloading the price history.
history.needsBackfill: To see the portfolio evolution you need to download the price history.
history.fxMissing: FX history is missing: USD/GBP/CHF values are converted with an approximate rate. Download the history to fix this.
history.partialHistory: The available history doesn't cover the portfolio's full life; the chart shows the available range.

analytics.title: Portfolio analytics
analytics.needsBackfill: Historical data hasn't been downloaded yet. Required to compute the metrics.
analytics.noData: Not enough historical data to compute the metrics. Try downloading the history.
analytics.disclaimer: Computed over {{weeks}} weeks with your current allocation applied retrospectively. Covers {{pct}}% of portfolio value.
analytics.tipBeta: Sensitivity of the portfolio to the market. Beta=1 means it moves with the benchmark; >1 more volatile, <1 less.
analytics.tipAlpha: Excess return that isn't explained by market risk. Positive alpha = portfolio beats what its risk would predict.
analytics.tipSharpe: Return per unit of total risk. >1 is good, >2 excellent, <0 means risk-free would have been better.
analytics.tipVolatility: Annualised standard deviation of returns. Higher = bigger swings.
analytics.tipMaxDD: Worst peak-to-trough drop in the analysis window. A measure of the historical worst case.
analytics.tipRSquared: How much of the portfolio's movement is explained by the market (0-100%). 100% = identical to benchmark.
analytics.tipExcluded: Tickers with under 6 months of history or no Yahoo data. Their weight is redistributed to the included ones.

fifo.title: FIFO calculator
fifo.intro: If you sell in several batches or at different prices, compute the realized result here using the FIFO method (shares bought first are sold first). Enter the operations in chronological order; each sell's result is what goes in the «Resultat» column.
fifo.oversold: Selling more shares than you hold
